description: M6: latency and throughput the gateway adds to one tool call
framing: Single machine: a shared cloud container (KVM guest), not isolated from other tenants, with no CPU pinning or frequency control. Numbers are indicative and vary run to run. Audit fsync cost depends entirely on the disk under the temp dir. Nothing here is compared with any other system. 'added' latency is handle_call time minus the median time of calling the no-op tool directly. Stage timings are the public components timed one by one with the same inputs; they need not sum to the pipeline. In-process threads share one GIL, so thread counts above 1 measure contention, not parallel speed-up.

method.gc: left on; gc.collect() before each timed loop
method.fsync_off: os.fsync replaced by a no-op for the audit log only; SQLite keeps its own syncs (default rollback journal, synchronous=FULL)
method.clock: real time.time for tokens and policy, time.time_ns for the audit log
method.gateway_options: library defaults (tool runs on the calling thread, no in-flight limit) unless stated; 'server_options' matches toolgate.server.build

ed25519_signature_only.label: Ed25519 signature check alone (part of every verify)

http.server: toolgate.server.create_app on uvicorn 0.54.0, 1 worker process, 127.0.0.1, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive
http.client: httpx 0.28.1, one httpx.Client (one connection) per client thread, in a separate process from the server

mcp_proxy.transport: in-process ASGI (httpx2.ASGITransport), no socket; the upstream is examples/mcp_upstream_server.py; MCP SDK client mcp.Client
mcp_proxy.note: added_p50_us is a difference of medians, not a distribution
